| Laurel B. Clark | December 8, 1994 | STS-107 (July 2003) | ~9 years |
| David M. Brown | December 8, 1994 | STS-107 (July 2003) | ~9 years |

- The shortest interval was **Kalpana Chawla** at approximately 3 years between selection and her first flight (STS-87)
- All STS-107 crew members exceeded the two-year threshold for introductory training
- This aligns with NASA's standard training program, which typically requires approximately 2-3 years for basic astronaut training, with additional time needed for mission-specific preparation, especially during the ISS era

Therefore, there are **no crew members** from the STS-107 mission who meet the criteria of receiving less than two years of introductory training after NASA selection.
